abstract_evidence_excerpt: The widespread presence of antibiotics in aquatic sediments, together with hypoxic conditions, constrains oxygen-driven natural degradation, thereby prolonging their environmental persistence. In this work, nitrate-intercalated layered double hydroxide (NO3-LDH) was employed as a controlled-release nitrate amendment to alleviate interfacial oxygen limitation while minimizing the secondary environmental risks associated with the high release peaks
